text:
You're creating solutions for AI current redundancies which will be streamlined as time passes nullifying the entire system and making your own even more redundant. This would be fine for trying to run a one man business band for now, but updates will naturally break it. Agents and bots will eventually be built in, executed, and logic applied based on complexity of the task based on the users request. 

To simplify this: it's like having a hard drive, processor, graphics card, ram, power supply, motherboard, and case be individual bots/agents talking to each other without actually being built in together with each other. AI will evolve to be a computer. There won't be a need for agents/bots

@Slimshady68356 True. And I do use these things. But they were trained on our data (our prose, our poetry, our art, our workflows, our movements, our specialized domain knowledge, our photos) without our consent and at first without even our knowledge. Therefore I believe they belong to us all, and they should not be moated or proprietary. Culture belongs to everybody, and LLMs are trained on and comprised of human culture. That is why I support open source / open weight models, and I use them as much as possible.

They’re getting better. The goal is to one day turn off my Claude and Chat subscriptions entirely, and be missing out on nothing at all. Honestly I get great results from the open models, that day is likely nigh at hand actually.
